**Blake Tollison Shelton** (born June 18, 1976)[[1]] is an American singer, songwriter, and television personality. In 2001, he made his debut with the single "[Austin] "Austin (Blake Shelton song)")" from his [self-titled debut album] "Blake Shelton (album)"). "Austin" spent five weeks at number one on the _[Billboard] "Billboard (magazine)")_[Hot Country Songs] chart. The now [platinum]-certified debut album also produced two more top-20 entries ("All Over Me" and "Ol' Red").[[1]]

His second and third albums, 2003's _[The Dreamer] "The Dreamer (Blake Shelton album)")_ and 2004's _[Blake Shelton's Barn & Grill]_, are gold and platinum, respectively.[[1]] His fourth album, _[Pure BS]_ (2007), was reissued in 2008 with a [cover] of [Michael Bublé]'s pop hit "[Home] "Home (Michael Bublé song)")" as one of the bonus tracks.[[2]] His fifth album, _[Startin' Fires]_ was released in November 2008.[[1]] It was followed by the extended plays _[Hillbilly Bone]_ and _[All About Tonight] "All About Tonight (EP)")_ in 2010 and the albums _[Red River Blue]_ in 2011,[[3]]_[Based on a True Story...]_ in 2013, _[Bringing Back the Sunshine]_ in 2014, _[If I'm Honest]_ in 2016, _[Texoma Shore]_ in 2017, _[Fully Loaded: God's Country]_ in 2019, _[Body Language] "Body Language (Blake Shelton album)")_ in 2021, and his latest album _[For Recreational Use Only]_ in 2025.

As of December 2020[[update]], Shelton has charted 41 singles, including 30 number ones,[[4]] 17 of which were consecutive. The 11th number one ("Doin' What She Likes") broke "the record for the most consecutive number-one singles in the Country Airplay chart's 24-year history".[[5]] Throughout his career, he has received nine [Grammy Award] nominations, including two for [Best Country Album].[[6]] In 2024, Shelton left Warner Music Nashville and signed with [BBR Music Group].

Shelton has been a judge on the televised singing competitions _[Nashville Star]_ and _[Clash of the Choirs]_, and a coach on NBC's _[The Voice] "The Voice (American TV series)")_. He was on _The Voice_ from 2011 to 2023, and in 9 of 23 seasons (2–4, 7, 11, 13, 18, 20, and 22), a member of his team won.

## Early life

[[edit]]

Blake Tollison Shelton was born on June 18, 1976, in [Ada, Oklahoma], to Dorothy Ann (née Byrd), a beauty salon owner, and Richard Lee "Dick" Shelton, a car salesman. Shelton began singing at an early age and by the age of 12, he was taught how to play the guitar by his uncle.[[7]] By age 15, he had written his first song. By age 16, he had received a Denbo Diamond Award in his home state.[[1]] On November 13, 1990, his older brother, Richie Shelton died in an automobile accident at the age of 24.[[8]]

After graduating from high school at 17, he moved to [Nashville, Tennessee], to pursue a singing career. There, he got a job at a music publishing company, and, in 1997, he was aided by [Bobby Braddock] to obtain a production contract with [Sony Music].[[9]]

Warner released Shelton's [self-titled debut album] "Blake Shelton (album)"), which was produced by songwriter Bobby Braddock.
